drafted_from: tool:seed-a-servers-receptionist's row in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/tool-rows.json, do-work/renew-a-tls-certificate.mjs, do-work/tls-host-owner.py and the tests in test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Seed the receptionist on my server at 192.0.2.34 with the newest release its feed names for x86_64 Linux." It runs tool:seed-a-servers-receptionist and answers where it placed the program.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it takes one server's facts as its input and answers what that server's certificate owner reports.
instructions: 1. Gather the server's facts: its public name, IPv4 address, SSH port, the administrator you sign in as, its pinned key ("<address> ssh-ed25519 <key>") and its layout (host: owner path, state folder, downloads folder, ingress, receptionist). The README in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/ shows a made-up one.

2. Say to your AI the sentence in start_here. It calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:seed-a-servers-receptionist and that input (the worked example shows one). The door mounts your server administration key for the run; you paste no key.

3. Read what comes back: {"seeded": true, "commit", "sequence", "binary"}; pass binary as receptionistBinary to tool:write-a-public-hosts-paths. An {"error": ...} or a thrown message names what to change (for example the layout or the pinned key was refused).
4. host.receptionist.releases is required (folder, program, feed urls over https and 64-hex public keys, target, body_max_bytes); a host with none answers "This host follows no release feed".

worked_examples.title: Seed from a feed with three entries
worked_examples.given: From tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/test/tls-host-owner.test.py (a seed is the newest release for the target with the program alone at its root): the feed names sequence 3 (commit e x40) and sequence 9 (commit d x40) for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and sequence 99 for aarch64; the newest of this target wins.
